post-fd-navier-slip-wall-law.physical_scope: An adopted smooth stationary impermeable wall law for the incompressible Newtonian branch; no universality, measured coefficient, roughness derivation, or moving-wall slip law is asserted.

post-fd-navier-slip-wall-law:
## Postulate

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded domain with $C^2$ boundary, fixed in an inertial Euclidean frame, and let $n$ be its outward unit normal. On $\partial\Omega$, let $u$ be the trace of a $C^1$ fluid-velocity field in metres per second and let $\sigma$ be the Cauchy-stress tensor in pascals, with traction on the fluid defined by $\sigma n$. For a vector $a$, define its tangential projection by $a_\tau:=a-(a\cdot n)n$. Adopt impermeability $u\cdot n=0$ and the linear friction wall law

$$ (\sigma n)_\tau=-\beta u_\tau,$$

where $\beta\ge0$ is a constant with units pascal-seconds per metre. In the incompressible Newtonian branch with constant dynamic viscosity $\eta>0$ in pascal-seconds, this law corresponds for finite slip length $\ell_s>0$ to $\beta=\eta/\ell_s$; $\beta=0$ is the zero-tangential-traction endpoint. This is a selected wall model, not a consequence of interior balance equations, a measured value of $\beta$, or a claim that any material or wall universally obeys it.

pthm-fd-local-momentum-balance-from-cont.physical_scope: Smooth positive-density constant-density incompressible Newtonian material regions under the adopted integral momentum balance. It derives the local forced momentum equation by transport and localization; it asserts no solution existence or empirical validity.

pthm-fd-local-momentum-balance-from-cont:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open reference region. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times B;\mathbb R^3)$ be a material motion whose maps $\chi_t$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their open images, and define the Eulerian velocity by $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$. Assume that $\partial_tu$ and all spatial derivatives of $u$ through order two are continuous on $\mathcal O$, that $p$ and its spatial first derivatives are continuous on $\mathcal O$, and that $b\in C^0(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^3)$; here $u$ is in metres per second, $p$ in pascals, and body acceleration $b$ in metres per second squared. In the selected constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch, let the current density be the constant $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, let $\operatorname{div}u=0$, let the dynamic viscosity be the constant $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds, and put

$$D(u):=\frac{\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}}2,\qquad \sigma:=-pI_3+2\eta D(u),\qquad (\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}.$$

Assume the adopted material linear-momentum balance holds for every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with $C^1$ boundary:

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(V)}\sigma n\,dS,$$

where $n$ is the outward normal and $dx,dS$ are Euclidean volume and area measures. Then throughout each $\Omega_t$ the corresponding local equation is

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b.$$

This is a conditional local form of the adopted balance for the stated smooth material motion and model branch; it makes no existence or empirical-applicability claim.

pthm-fd-wall-mechanical-power-balance.physical_scope: Smooth incompressible Newtonian solutions of constant positive density and viscosity on a fixed bounded C2 domain, or on the stated periodic channel with no-slip physical walls. The adopted stationary Navier friction law is used only on the bounded-domain branch. It gives conditional mechanical power identities and stationary bounded-domain smooth uniqueness only; no existence or universal wall-law applicability is asserted.

pthm-fd-wall-mechanical-power-balance:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice, meaning every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $T>0$ seconds. The spatial domain is either (B) a bounded connected nonempty open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ with $C^2$ boundary, or (P) a periodic channel $\Omega_{L_x,h,L_z}:=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times(0,h)\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$ with $L_x,L_z,h>0$ metres. In (P), fields and the material motion are periodic in the first and third coordinates on the Euclidean covering space, and the only physical wall boundary is $\Gamma=(\mathbb R/L_x\mathbb Z)\times\{0,h\}\times(\mathbb R/L_z\mathbb Z)$; identified periodic faces are not walls. In (B), set $\Gamma:=\partial\Omega$. In either case let $n$ be the outward unit normal on $\Gamma$, let $dx$ be Euclidean volume measure (or its periodic-cell quotient measure), and let $dS$ be the induced area measure on $\Gamma$. Let the constant mass density be $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, the constant dynamic viscosity be $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds, the body-acceleration field be $b\in C([0,T]\times\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ in metres per second squared, the velocity be $u\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second, and the pressure be $p\in C([0,T];C^1(\overline\Omega))$ in pascals. Assume that $u$ is the Eulerian velocity of a smooth material motion preserving $\Omega$ (or its periodic lift), and that the adopted material linear-momentum balance holds on every admissible material subregion. Define $D(u)_{ij}:=(\partial_{x_j}u_i+\partial_{x_i}u_j)/2$, $\sigma:=-pI+2\eta D(u)$, and rowwise $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. At every time impose one of the following wall laws: (N) no-slip, $u=g$ on $\Gamma$ for a prescribed tangential wall-velocity field $g\in C^1([0,T];C^2(\Gamma;\mathbb R^3))$ in metres per second with $g\cdot n=0$; or (S) stationary Navier friction on branch (B) only, $u\cdot n=0$ and $(\sigma n)_\tau=-\beta u_\tau$ on $\Gamma$, where $a_\tau:=a-(a\cdot n)n$ and $\beta\ge0$ is the adopted constant wall coefficient in pascal-seconds per metre. Then the local momentum equation

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b,\qquad \operatorname{div}u=0$$

holds on the fluid domain by the local momentum result from the adopted material balance. Let $K(t):=\int_\Omega \rho|u(t,x)|^2/2\,dx$. Then for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (N),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx+\int_{\Gamma}g\cdot\sigma n\,dS,$$

and for every $t\in(0,T)$ in case (S),

$$\frac{dK}{dt}=\int_\Omega \rho b\cdot u\,dx-2\eta\int_\Omega |D(u)|^2\,dx-\beta\int_{\Gamma}|u_\tau|^2\,dS.$$

Every term has units of watts. In branch (B) only, in either stationary homogeneous case, (N) with $g=0$ or (S) with a fixed $\beta$, there is at most one solution in this smooth class for a given body force and initial velocity. These are deductions conditional on the stated model and wall assumptions; no solution-existence or empirical-applicability claim is made.

pthm-fd-linear-acoustic-model-prediction.physical_scope: Exact global smooth tangent-model prediction for a positive-density, no-force barotropic Euler equilibrium at rest on a periodic three-dimensional cell, when p'(rho*)>0. No finite-amplitude error estimate or empirical applicability claim is asserted.

pthm-fd-linear-acoustic-model-prediction:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds with $0\in I$, let $L=1\,\mathrm m$, and let $\Omega_L:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$ be a spatial periodic cell with coordinates in metres and volume measure $dx$ induced from a fundamental cell. Let $p:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a $C^1$ barotropic pressure law in pascals, let $\rho_*>0$ be a constant reference density in kilograms per cubic metre, and assume $p'(\rho_*)>0$ in square metres per second squared. The adopted no-force barotropic Euler model is

$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)+\nabla p(\rho)=0,$$

for periodic fields $\rho\in C^2(I\times\Omega_L;(0,\infty))$ and $u\in C^2(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R^3)$, where density is in kilograms per cubic metre and velocity is in metres per second. The uniform state $(\rho,u)=(\rho_*,0)$ is an equilibrium. For $z\in C^\infty(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R)$ and $v\in C^\infty(I\times\Omega_L;\mathbb R^3)$ periodic in space, define the tangent model as the vanishing first variation at $\epsilon=0$ of this equation operator on $\rho_\epsilon=\rho_*+\epsilon z$ and $u_\epsilon=\epsilon v$. That tangent model is

$$\partial_t z+\rho_*\operatorname{div}v=0,\qquad \partial_t v+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*}\nabla z=0,\qquad (z,v)|_{t=0}=(z_0,v_0),\qquad c_*:=\sqrt{p'(\rho_*)}>0.$$

Here $z$ is a density perturbation in kilograms per cubic metre, $v$ is a velocity perturbation in metres per second, and $c_*$ is the model sound speed in metres per second. For every smooth periodic initial pair $z_0:\Omega_L\to\mathbb R$ and $v_0:\Omega_L\to\mathbb R^3$, this linear tangent system has a unique global smooth solution $(z,v):\mathbb R\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$. Its acoustic energy

$$E_{\mathrm{ac}}(t):=\frac12\int_{\Omega_L}\left(\rho_*|v|^2+\frac{c_*^2}{\rho_*}z^2\right)\,dx$$

is constant in joules. For each nonzero periodic wavevector $\kappa\in L^{-1}\mathbb Z^3$ in inverse metres, longitudinal Fourier modes with angular frequency $\omega$ in inverse seconds satisfy $\omega^2=c_*^2|\kappa|^2$; zero-frequency mean and transverse velocity modes are constant. These are exact deductions for the specified linear tangent model, not a finite-amplitude approximation theorem, an observation, or a claim that an actual fluid follows the model.

ex-fd-adopted-poiseuille-couette.physical_scope: Exact steady profiles in the stated periodic incompressible Newtonian channel model with no-slip walls; the Poiseuille pressure-drop notation is replaced by a constant body acceleration on the periodic cell. No measured flow or claim about a named material is included.
